questions.q: Why use Athena to aggregate before loading data into pandas?
options: Only a small aggregated result has to travel to your notebook
Athena trains the model for you
pandas cannot read Parquet
Athena queries are always free
questions.explain: SQL can filter and aggregate in place, so only a small result reaches your notebook. Athena bills by data scanned, so it is not free.

questions.q: What is the drawback of TABLESAMPLE BERNOULLI for an experiment you want to repeat?
options: It only works on CSV files
It always returns the same rows
It is random, so two runs return different rows
It deletes the rows it does not select
questions.explain: BERNOULLI keeps each row with a given probability, so results vary between runs. Filtering on a key such as customer_id % 10 = 0 returns the same rows each time.

questions.q: What does the AWS documentation say about the external_location of a CTAS query?
options: It may already contain data; Athena overwrites it
It must be a local disk path
It is required for every query
It must contain no data, because Athena never deletes your data
questions.explain: If you reuse a location that already holds data, the CTAS query fails. Athena never attempts to delete your data, so you must clear the location yourself.

questions.q: In this lesson, why was the SQL run in SQLite?
options: SQLite is the engine underneath Athena
No AWS account is used, so SQLite served as a labeled local stand-in
SQLite is faster than Athena on large data
Athena cannot run GROUP BY
questions.explain: The lesson uses SQLite as a stand-in because Athena cannot be called here. Plain SELECT, GROUP BY and CASE agree, but details differ, so retest on Athena.

questions.q: Which habit lowers Athena cost, given that it bills by data scanned?
options: Always use SELECT *
Select only the needed columns and store tables as Parquet
Store training tables as uncompressed CSV
Run every query twice to be safe
questions.explain: Columnar Parquet plus selecting only the columns you need reduces the bytes scanned, and therefore cost.
